ledger.x: c. 1110: the Meitei kingdom of Kangleipak at Imphal. The court chronicle 'dates the first king to 33 CE' (Parratt and Kamei suspect astrology, and the first seven kings are said to reign to 411 CE); the Loiyamba Shinyen, Manipur's 'first written constitution', is 'dated to 1110 ad' (the page also says early 12th and…
1709: under Gharib Niwaz (Pamheiba, 1709-1748) 'the kingdom's name changed from Kangleipak to Manipur'.
1826: the Burmese are out of Manipur 'and then from Kabaw Valley by 1826' (History: the occupation 1819-1826).
1834: the Kabaw Valley goes back to Burma 'after prolonged negotiation' (some Manipuri scholars call it a lease); Manipur received Rs 6,370 a year as compensation.

The hill areas: the Kingdom page gives 22,327 km2 'in the 20th century' (the extent of the Manipur of the grid) and mentions the Naga and Kuki hill areas disturbed after 1891, but no page opened says when the hill country came under the kings.
27 April 1891: 'the Silchar, Tamu and Kohima columns united, capturing Imphal after finding it deserted'; the Kingdom page says the British briefly annexed Manipur under the doctrine of lapse.
27 April 1891: the war ends with the fall of Imphal.
22 September 1891: 'the British placed the young boy Meidingngu Churachand on the throne'; Manipur 'was converted into an Indian princely state subject to British Paramountcy'.
15 October 1949: the kingdom merges with India.

wars.name: Seven Years Devastation (Burmese occupation of Manipur)
wars.outcome: Burmese forces occupied Manipur 1819-1826; Gambhir Singh, helped by the British, expelled them from Manipur and the Kabaw Valley by 1826.

wars.name: Anglo-Manipur War
wars.outcome: 31 March - 27 April 1891: Imphal captured; Tikendrajit hanged 13 August 1891; Churachand placed on the throne 22 September 1891; Manipur a princely state.

certainty.note: A valley kingdom with hill tribute lands; no page opened gives a boundary.
The Kabaw Valley frontier with Burma was settled in 1834 by agreement (page: 'restored to Burma after prolonged negotiation'); the hill boundaries are not drawn on any page.
